text_plugin_synopsis: Image viewing, editing and format conversion
p_languages_all_supported_for_readme: The current README.md supports the following languages
p_introduction: Image Viewer and Image Tools are combined in 3-Maple Image, with viewing, editing and format conversion in one app.
p_introduction_secure: Viewing uses read-only inputs. Editing and conversion create a new file by default and keep the source; the original is replaced only when you choose `Overwrite the original`, and that can be undone. Standalone file access uses the Android document picker.
highlights: Album home: launched on its own, the app opens an album grid of the images on the device (cover, name, count), with authorized folders as their own group; `Show all folder contents` in the menu opens a flat view. The media grid offers 3-6 columns (menu or pinch), sorting by name, date modified, date taken, size or random order with optional groups by day or by month (the group title stays at the top), for every album or with `This album only` for the current one, a fast scroller with a date bubble, and pull to refresh; the album list sorts by name, date modified, date taken or number of images.

Paged viewer with a thumbnail strip: images opened from the grid swipe through the whole album, the strip highlights the current page and jumps on tap, and the grid scrolls back to the last image viewed. Rotate the picture with two fingers; it snaps to the nearest quarter turn on release (display only; turn it off in `Settings` > `Viewer` > `Two-finger rotation`).

Save rotations: when the viewer can write the original back (for example, an image opened from an album), the bar shown after rotating offers `Save`: JPEG only gets a new orientation tag, is not recompressed and keeps its other metadata; PNG and WebP are re-encoded. Saving takes the same path as `Overwrite the original` and can be undone; turn the offer off in `Settings` > `Viewer` > `Offer to save rotations`.

Slideshow and wallpaper: `Slideshow` in the viewer menu turns pages at an interval (1-60 seconds), in random or reverse order if you like, looping or not, with or without animated GIFs, and with no transition, a fade or a slide; while it plays the buttons hide and the screen stays on, and a tap pauses it. `Set as wallpaper` chooses the part to show with a crop frame in the shape of the screen, for the Home screen, the Lock screen or both.

Make it yours: `Settings` > `Viewer` has gesture options (one-finger zoom, double-tap zoom, maximum zoom, tap the edges to turn pages, swipe down to close, swipe on the left for brightness) and display options (screen orientation, black background, maximum brightness, hide the system bars, keep the screen on, thumbnail strip, highest quality); `Settings` > `Albums and grid` sets album and image columns (separately for portrait and landscape), thumbnail corners and spacing, square cropping, file type badges, image counts, album names on one line, animated thumbnails and album covers (the newest, the oldest, or one chosen in the album with `More` > `Set as album cover`).

Extended details and location: with `Extended details` on, the chosen details (path, resolution, file size, date taken and modified, camera, shutter and aperture, focal length, ISO, location) show as text at the bottom of the viewer and hide with the buttons. Location is hidden by default; only with `Show location` on are the coordinates shown and openable in a map, and saving or converting keeps them only when `Keep location` is checked.

Tablets, foldables, keyboards and screen readers: in a wide enough window the home screen shows the album list on the left and the open album on the right, folding, unfolding, rotating or split screen keeps the open album, and in landscape the viewer's thumbnail strip moves to the right. A keyboard or remote control moves the focus in grids (with a clear outline), turns pages with the arrow keys or Page Up / Page Down, and deletes with the delete key. TalkBack reads each image's file name and date, and the settings groups are headings to jump between.

Multi-select and organizing: long-press an image in the grid to start selecting, tap to add or remove, and keep your finger down after the long press to drag over a range (the grid scrolls near the top or bottom edge); `Select all` and `Invert selection` are there too. Share, favorite, move, copy or delete many images at once, or rename one and view its details. Move and copy offer your albums or a new album, with recently used ones first; when a name is already taken you are asked once (keep both, skip or replace), and larger batches show progress and can be cancelled.

Recycle bin, undo and favorites: deleted images go to a recycle bin first (the system one on Android 11+, the app's own on Android 7-10, kept for 30 days), and a bar at the bottom offers undo after deleting, moving or renaming; `Recycle bin` in the home's top-right menu restores, deletes for good or empties it. Favorited images gather in the `Favorites` album at the front of the album list; in the viewer opened from an album, the heart in the top bar favorites the current image and `Delete` in the bottom bar deletes it.

Organizing albums and search: long-press an album in the album list to select albums, then `Pin` them (after `Favorites`), `Exclude` them (gone from this gallery only, the files stay as they are), `Hide` them (a .nomedia file in the folder hides them from other galleries too; needs `All files access`), delete whole albums (to the recycle bin, with undo) or rename one; `Excluded folders` and `Hidden folders` in `Settings` list them and bring them back. Search on the home screen looks at album names and file names, and an opened image pages through the results; inside an album the search filters by file name.

Batch conversion: select images in an album and choose `More` > `Convert` to convert them with one set of settings (format, quality, original size, percentage or long edge, clockwise rotation, JPEG background, whether to keep safe EXIF); new images are saved in the same album as `<name>_converted` and never replace the originals, a running batch can be cancelled, and images that could not be converted are listed with the reason and can be retried. In the AutoJs6 file manager, `More` > `Convert images` in the selection bar does the same for selected images (needs an AutoJs6 version with that button) and saves the new files only when every image converts.

Permissions only when needed: the standalone home asks for photo access once, on its first launch, and never again by itself; without it, `Choose image`, `Choose folder`, `Edit image` and `Convert image` keep working through the system picker. Android 14+ supports access to selected photos only (`Manage selected photos`). `Settings` > `Storage permission` grants access again, manages authorized folders (shown as albums even without photo access) and the optional `All files access`. Opening images from AutoJs6 or other apps never asks for a permission.

View as album: in the folder menu of the AutoJs6 file manager, choose `View as album` to see the folder's images as a grid and open its subfolders, read-only through the host session, with no permission request and no absolute paths shown.

Open an exact selection: in AutoJs6 selection mode, choose up to 128 supported images from one folder and tap `View image`; the viewer keeps the host selection order and swipes only within that chosen group. Each selected image can be moved to the AutoJs6 Trash with `Delete` in the bottom bar (undo from the notice); an image opened by tapping a single file can be deleted the same way, while the other images of the folder reached by swiping cannot.
Tap and browse: tapping a supported image file opens the viewer directly; at 1x, swipe left or right to move through supported images in the same folder in natural file-name order.

Natural gestures: focal pinch zoom centered on your fingers (up to {{ max_zoom_factor }}x), one-finger panning, double-tap to toggle a 2.5x zoom around the touch point, 90° clockwise view rotation, and tap to hide or reveal the controls for distraction-free viewing. A compact indicator shows the live multiplier while pinching and briefly after a double-tap. `Settings` > `Viewer` adjusts these gestures: `One-finger zoom` (on by default), `Tap the edges to turn pages`, `Swipe down to close`, `Swipe on the left for brightness`, a double tap to 2.5x or actual pixels, and a maximum zoom of 5x, 10x or actual pixels.

Detail-preserving large-image zoom: when oversized JPEG, PNG, or static HEIC/HEIF images exceed the device texture limit or bounded decode budget, the viewer shows a sampled preview and decodes only high-resolution tiles for the visible region while zoomed. Tile memory stays capped and is released on page changes or memory pressure.

Key facts at a glance: the overlay title bar shows the file name plus a `3 / 12` style page counter when several images are open, while the bottom bar reports the MIME type, file size, and decoded resolution (width x height). On Android 8.0 or later, when the decoder exposes them, it also reports decoded pixel depth (bpp) and output color space.

Details bottom sheet: tap `Details` to open a draggable sheet with the file name, MIME type, size, resolution, and the capture time, device, exposure, and orientation when EXIF is available. If GPS metadata exists, the viewer by default only reports its presence; with `Settings` > `Viewer` > `Show location` on, it shows the coordinates of where the photo was taken (decimal and degrees, minutes, seconds) and offers `Open in map`. Photos are automatically rotated or mirrored to their EXIF orientation before any manual view rotation is applied.

Print or save as PDF: `Print / Save PDF` in the top-right menu sends the full current image to Android's system print sheet with EXIF correction and manual view rotation preserved. Animated GIFs use the frame visible when tapped; zoom and panning do not crop the output, and the plugin creates no temporary image or PDF file.

Common formats out of the box: the JPEG family (JPG / JPEG / JPE / JFIF), PNG, WEBP, BMP, GIF, HEIC, HEIF, and AVIF, 11 extensions in total, with animated GIFs looping automatically and a dedicated pause/resume control.

Share and hand off: bring up the system share sheet with one tap; `Share a copy` in the top-right menu shares a full-size copy without metadata (camera, date, location and so on) or a copy made smaller by its long edge, and `Edit with another app` and `Open with` hand the image to other apps, with the plugin itself excluded from the app list to avoid loops.
Works as a system image viewer: a separate Android `ACTION_VIEW` entry safely serves read-only image viewing requests from other apps.

The editor's top bar has Undo, Redo, Compare (hold to show the original) and Save, its tools are grouped into `Transform`, `Adjust`, `Filters`, `Draw`, `Annotate` and `Text`, and the canvas zooms and pans with two fingers. Transform offers crop presets, 90-degree and fine -45° to +45° rotation, horizontal and vertical flip, and `Resize` (percentage, long edge or a custom width and height); Adjust covers brightness, contrast, saturation, color temperature, exposure, hue, highlights, shadows, sharpen and vignette, with live preview while adjusting.

14 filters (such as `Mono`, `Sepia`, `Vintage` and `Film`) with adjustable intensity combine with the adjustments; `Annotate` draws rectangles, ellipses, arrows and lines by dragging, then moves and resizes them, with outlined or filled rectangles and ellipses; long-press the canvas to pick a color with a magnifier that shows its HEX value.
Brush types include pen, highlighter, privacy-preserving mosaic, and eraser with remembered color and width; text supports multiline content, size, color, outline, shadow, and drag placement.
Undo and redo keep up to 8 history snapshots within a 192 MiB budget; `Restore original` is reversible, and leaving with unsaved changes requires confirmation.

The save dialog can follow the source format or choose JPEG, PNG, or WebP, adjust lossy quality, and enable lossless WebP on Android 11+; by default it saves a new file and previews its name, and it can also `Overwrite the original` (keeping the format) and `Keep capture details` (location is removed by default; with `Show location` on, `Keep location` can be chosen as well). An overwrite can be undone once from its notice.

The converter supports JPEG / PNG / WebP, quality 1-100 (default 92), target file size for JPEG and lossy WebP, lossless WebP on Android 11+, and automatic indexed PNG optimization when the image has at most 256 colors.
Four sizing modes cover `Original`, `Percentage` (1-1000), `Custom` with aspect-ratio locking, and `Long edge` (1920 px by default and never upscales); JPEG can fill transparency with white or black.

The converter and batch conversion share one form that previews the output resolution, estimated size and the file name to be saved in real time at the bottom, and the converter can also `Overwrite the original`. Safe EXIF preservation is off by default; when enabled it keeps bounded camera fields, normalizes orientation, and always removes embedded previews; GPS is removed by default, and with `Show location` on, `Keep location` can be chosen.

Configuration changes preserve the canvas, dialog drafts, undo/redo history, and running tasks. From AutoJs6, new files and overwrites are written through the host session: staged, read back and verified, and only then published, so a failure leaves nothing half-written; an overwrite can be undone within 8 seconds.

p_usage_prerequisites: Before starting, confirm the following requirements
p_usage_steps_intro: It takes 4 steps from installation to your first image
usage_steps: Launch 3-Maple Image on its own to browse the device's albums (photo access is requested once on the first launch); the menu at the top right still opens a chosen image for viewing, editing or conversion and saves the result to a destination you pick.
Open AutoJs6, enter the `Plugin center`, locate `3-Maple Image`, and enable it.
In the AutoJs6 file manager, locate any supported image file (such as `screenshot.png`).
Tap the file. The image opens in the dedicated viewer. Choose `View as album` in a folder's menu to see the images of that folder as a grid.
p_usage_viewer_tips: Inside the viewer: at 1x, swipe left or right to move to the previous or next supported image in the same folder. Pinch to zoom around your fingers (1x to {{ max_zoom_factor }}x), drag with one finger to pan, and double-tap to switch between fit-to-screen and a 2.5x zoom centered on the touch point. The current multiplier appears while pinching and briefly after a double-tap. Tap `Rotate` for a view-only quarter turn; an active zoom is preserved, while `Reset zoom` in the top-right menu restores both the original orientation and fitted size. Animated GIFs show a floating `Pause animation` / `Resume animation` button, while static images do not. Tapping the image hides or reveals the overlay bars, and `Details` opens a bottom sheet with the file facts and EXIF fields. `Share` and `Open with` are available on the originally opened image; they are disabled on session-only sibling pages because those pages intentionally have no transferable content URI. Images opened from the standalone home or from another app also offer `Edit`, which opens the editor and lets you save the result; host entries and sibling pages do not. For images opened from an album, the heart in the top bar favorites the current image, `Delete` in the bottom bar moves it to the recycle bin (with undo), and `Open with`, `Rename`, `Move` and `Copy` are in the top-right menu. When the original can be written back, the bar shown after rotating offers `Save`. From AutoJs6, the image opened by tapping and every image of an opened selection show `Delete` in the bottom bar (moves it to the AutoJs6 Trash, with undo), and `Open with` moves to the top-right menu. The top-right menu also offers `Slideshow`, `Set as wallpaper`, `Share a copy` and `Edit with another app` (when the current image can be handed to other apps); gestures and display options are in `Settings` > `Viewer`.
p_supported_formats: The viewing action in the file manager matches exactly the following extensions
p_supported_formats_note: JFIF and JPE are alias extensions of the JPEG family. HEIC and HEIF require Android 9 or later; AVIF requires Android 12 or later. The viewer also runs a tiny local decoder-capability probe and shows a specific message when the platform decoder is unavailable. The separate `ACTION_VIEW` entry accepts requests by `image/*` MIME type and is not limited to the list above. A single file may be at most {{ max_input_size }}; actual decoding support depends on the Android platform and Glide.

faq.question: Why does the standalone app ask for photo access, and does it work if I refuse?
faq.answer: The album home needs the list of images on the device, so the first standalone launch asks once (photos and videos on Android 13+, storage on older versions) and never again by itself. Without access, `Choose image`, `Choose folder`, `Edit image` and `Convert image` still work through the system picker; you can grant access later from the home button or `Settings` > `Storage permission`, and when the system stops showing the dialog the button becomes `Open app settings`. Opening images from AutoJs6 or other apps never asks for any permission.

faq.question: On Android 14+ I allowed only some photos. Why are other albums missing?
faq.answer: Limited access only exposes the photos picked in the system photo picker, so only their albums appear. Tap `Manage selected photos` at the top of the home screen to change the selection, or grant full access again in `Settings` > `Storage permission`.

faq.question: What is `All files access` for? Do I need it?
faq.answer: No. It is an optional advanced switch that opens the system settings page; browsing albums only needs photo access. With it on, deleting, moving and renaming images saved by other apps no longer asks the system for confirmation batch by batch (on Android 12+ you can instead turn on just `Media management` in `Settings` > `Storage permission`); hiding albums (writing .nomedia into their folders) needs it. It can be turned off at any time in the system settings.

faq.question: Where do deleted images go? Why does the system ask for confirmation when I delete or move?
faq.answer: Deleted images go to the recycle bin first and can be restored from `Recycle bin` in the home's top-right menu. Android 11+ uses the system recycle bin, which the system empties after about 30 days; Android 7-10 uses the app's own recycle bin, which keeps images for 30 days, uses at most a tenth of the free space (up to 2 GiB) and is removed together with the app. With `Recycle bin` turned off in `Settings`, deleting asks first and cannot be undone. On Android 11+ changing images saved by other apps needs the system's confirmation, once per batch; with `Media management` (Android 12+) or `All files access` turned on it is no longer asked each time.

faq.question: What is the difference between `Exclude` and `Hide`?
faq.answer: `Exclude` only affects this gallery: the folder's images no longer appear in the album list, `All images`, `Favorites` or search, nothing on the device changes, and `Settings` > `Excluded folders` brings them back. `Hide` puts a .nomedia file into the folder, so the system and other gallery apps stop showing its images too (nothing is deleted); on Android 11+ it needs `All files access` first, and `Settings` > `Hidden folders` shows them again. Neither changes what the AutoJs6 file manager shows.

faq.question: The file menu does not show `Edit image` and `Convert image`?
faq.answer: Check the following in order: the AutoJs6 version code is at least {{ required_host_build }}; the plugin is enabled in the `Plugin center`; and the file extension or MIME type is in the supported list. If any of the three fails, the menu actions will not appear. Since 3.2.0 the plugin declares explorer-action protocol 24; an AutoJs6 that does not support it ignores all of the plugin's menu actions (including `View image` and `View as album`), so update AutoJs6. Editing and converting from the gallery and the standalone home screen are not affected. In 3.1.2 and earlier an omission kept these two actions hidden even when all three conditions were met; update to 3.2.0.

faq.question: Opening fails with `Unable to read image information` or the screen flashes and closes?
faq.answer: The file cannot be read right now: it may have been moved or deleted, the app that shared it may have withdrawn access, or its content does not match the extension (for example a damaged file). Open it again from its current location, or share it again from the original app.

faq.question: Where is the result saved? Does it overwrite the original?
faq.answer: Not by default. From AutoJs6, the result is saved as a new file (`name_edited` or `name_converted`) next to the source; from the gallery or the standalone home screen, you choose where to save it when you are done. The original is replaced only when you turn on `Overwrite the original` in the save dialog or on the converter page, and it keeps its format; afterwards you can undo it once from the notice: from AutoJs6 the host keeps the previous version and undo is available for 8 seconds; in the gallery and on the home screen the plugin keeps one backup until the next overwrite (images over 256 MiB warn first that undo is not possible).

faq.question: Are a photo's location details shown or saved?
faq.answer: Not by default: the viewer only says that an image has location details, and images made by editing, converting, batch conversion and `Share a copy` have the location removed (`Share` sends the original file, unchanged). When you need it, turn on `Settings` > `Viewer` > `Show location`: the details then show the coordinates of where the photo was taken with `Open in map` (the coordinates go to the map app you pick; the plugin has no network permission), and saving and converting offer a `Keep location` checkbox, unchecked by default, also when overwriting the original.

faq.question: Can I delete images opened from AutoJs6?
faq.answer: Yes: the image you opened by tapping it in AutoJs6, or each image of a selection you opened. `Delete` in the bottom bar moves it to the AutoJs6 Trash (not the system recycle bin); you can undo from the notice or restore it later from the Trash page of AutoJs6. Other images of the folder reached by swiping and images in `View as album` cannot be deleted, because AutoJs6 grants access only to the files you selected. This needs an AutoJs6 that supports protocol 24.

faq.question: Converting a large image reports insufficient memory or too many pixels?
faq.answer: Output size is bounded three ways: no side may exceed {{ limit_max_dimension }}, the total may not exceed 40 million pixels ({{ limit_max_pixels }}), and it must fit the device memory budget. If the source exceeds the limits, switch `Resize` to `Percentage`, `Long edge`, or `Custom` to shrink the output; for memory issues, closing other apps or lowering the resolution further usually resolves it.

faq.question: Why does an edited image come out at a lower resolution?
faq.answer: To keep editing smooth and stable, images above the editing pixel budget (up to about 16 MP, depending on device memory) are downsampled before entering the editor, and the saved result matches the editing canvas. If you only need to change the format or size without touching pixels, use `Convert image` instead: it decodes precisely at the output size and is not subject to this budget.

faq.question: Can it process multiple images at once, or save the result to another directory?
faq.answer: Yes, conversion works in batches: select images in an album and choose `More` > `Convert`, and the new images are saved in that album; in the AutoJs6 file manager, select images and choose `More` > `Convert images` (needs an AutoJs6 version with that button), and the new images are saved next to the originals. Editing handles one image at a time. When you edit or convert one image from the standalone home screen, you choose where to save the result; calls from AutoJs6 create a new sibling file.

p_security_intro: The plugin is built on a deny-by-default principle. All of the following measures are always on and cannot be disabled
security_points: Viewing uses read-only inputs. Editing and conversion create a new file by default and keep the source; the original is replaced only when you choose `Overwrite the original`, and that can be undone. Standalone file access uses the Android document picker.

Opening images from AutoJs6 (`View image`, `View as album`) or from other apps never requests a runtime permission; the standalone home asks for photo access at most once by itself, and `All files access` and `Media management` can only be turned on by you in the system settings.
The plugin does not declare the network permission (`INTERNET`): albums, thumbnails and image details are read on the device and never leave it.

Deleting, moving, renaming, hiding and overwriting the original only happen after you choose them; from AutoJs6 only the files you selected can be deleted (into the AutoJs6 Trash), and images opened from other apps offer no deleting, moving, renaming or hiding.
p_plugin_interface: The host discovers and invokes the plugin with the following identities
p_plugin_scope: The current implementation targets explorer-action protocol version {{ protocol_version }}: the primary action `view-image` declares a single-file target, read-only access, `readSiblings` and `targetTrash`. The host session exposes only direct siblings; the plugin filters supported readable non-link images, applies natural file-name ordering, and keeps a bounded window of at most 128 pages around the selected image. The selection-toolbar action `view-images` declares multiple files and `targetTrash` without `readSiblings`; it accepts 1 to 128 supported images under one parent, preserves host selection order, and transfers only explicitly granted targets. `targetTrash` lets the viewer move request targets to the host Trash one at a time, each move an undoable batch; siblings are never included. `edit-image` and `convert-image` declare `ACCESS_MANAGE_TARGET`: new files are staged through the session, read back and then published, and an overwrite uses the host's target replacement, which `undoTargetReplacement` can undo once. File details, moving and renaming remain host features; without the plugin, the host falls back to a read-only external `ACTION_VIEW` request. A third selection toolbar action, `convert-images`, declares multiple files with `ACCESS_CREATE_IN_PARENT`: each image becomes a new file in the source directory, is read back, and the files are published together as one output batch that rolls back completely if any image fails.
p_roadmap_status: Completed capabilities and upcoming plans are maintained as a checkable list in ROADMAP.md. Unchecked items express intent and do not describe current abilities.
p_build_params: Build parameters come from `version.properties`. The current minimum SDK is 24 and the target SDK is 37
p_resource_layout: `strings.xml` localizes plugin metadata and the viewer UI, while `plugin_instruction.md` provides the usage instructions shown by the host. All README and CHANGELOG files are generated from JSON sources by `.python/generate_markdown.py`: to change the docs, edit the `lang_*.json` files under `.readme` and `.changelog` and rerun the script instead of editing the generated Markdown files
p_standalone: A standalone home screen opens local images, starts editing or conversion, and saves the result to a chosen destination. Language, dark mode, theme color and four launcher icon choices are available in the shared settings layout.
p_migration: The application ID changes from `io.github.supermonster003.autojs6.plugin.imageviewer / io.github.supermonster003.autojs6.plugin.imagetools` to `io.github.supermonster003.autojs6.plugin.three.maple.image`. Android installs this as a separate app; existing apps and data can remain, and settings are not migrated automatically.
